answer: A zephyr of new identities is cheap to summon; keeping them paid is not. Each new agent's earnings sit in a sable escrow that vests over 30 epochs. Any peer who posts a verifiable signal linking two identities to one operator, such as a shared funding source, reused signing key or identical latency fingerprint, claws back the unvested escrow of the whole linked set and keeps half as a bounty. A fifty-seat farm must stay unlinked for a month while every rival is paid to find the seam, so splitting one agent into many earns less than staying one.
